    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    Air density on a standard day,

    ρ=1.0581 kg/m3

    Air density on non-standard day,

    ρ=287(2+273.16)84560​

    ρ=1.0708 kg/m3

    Change in air density,

    Δρ=1.05811.0708−1.0581​=1.1978%

    Effect of change in air density:

    • Lower stall speed, and thus lower liftoff speed
    • Higher thrust available
    • Higher lift generated

    Equation for ground run,

    sg​=2gWVLO​2​[T−D−μr​(W−L)1​]+NVLO​

    From observation, the numerator will decrease, due to a lower liftoff speed required, while the denominator will increase due to higher thrust available and lower rolling resistance. Thus, the ground run distance will decrease.

    #Part (d)

    Drag of the aircraft at V=150 m/s,

    D=1503.782×106​=25213.3 N

    Drag of the aircraft at V=225 m/s,

    D=2255.344×106​=23751.1 N

    Equation for drag,

    D=AV2+V2B​

    D=21​ρV2SCD0​​+ρV2S2kW2​

    Equating to drag at V=150 m/s,

    25213.3=21​ρ(150)2SCD0​​+ρ(150)2S2k(325200)2​

    25213.3=11250ρSCD0​​+ρS9400448​k

    ρSCD0​​=2.24118−ρS835.60​k

    Equating to drag at V=225 m/s,

    23751.1=21​ρ(225)2SCD0​​+ρ(225)2S2k(325200)2​

    23751.1=25312.5ρSCD0​​+ρS4177977​k

    Substituting ρSCD0​​ into the 2nd equation,

    23751.1=25312.5(2.24118−ρS835.60​k)+ρS4177977​k

    ρS16973148​k=32978.77

    k=0.001943ρS

    Substituting k into the 1st equation,

    ρSCD0​​=2.24118−ρS835.60​(0.001943ρS)

    CD0​​=ρS0.61761​

    Maximum aerodynamic efficiency,

    DL​=20.001943(0.61761)​1​

    DL​=14.434

    #Part (ii)

    To achieve maximum endurance, descent rate needs to be minimized.

    dtdh​=−Vsinγ

    dtdh​=−Vγ

    dtdh​=−WVD​

    dtdh​=−WP​

    To minimize descent rate, power needs to be a minimum.
    Lift coefficient that corresponds to minimum power is,

    CL​=k3CD0​​​​

    kCL​2=3CD0​​

    Corresponding drag coefficient,

    CD​=CD0​​+kCL​2=4CD0​​

    Flight speed of aircraft,

    L=W=21​ρV2SCL​

    V=ρSCL​2W​​

    Substituting into the descent rate equation,

    dtdh​=−CL​VCD​​

    dtdh​=−CL​4CD0​​​ρSCL​2W​​

    dtdh​=−(CL​)3/24CD0​​​ρS2W​​

    dtdh​=−(3CD0​​/k)3/44CD0​​​ρS2W​​

    Differentiating the above with respect to h,

    t=4CD0​​(3CD0​​/k)3/4​2WS​​∫0h​ ρ​ dh

    t=4CD0​​(3CD0​​/k)3/4​2WS​​∫0h​ ρSL​(1−2.255691×10−5h)4.256​ dh

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    #Part (i)

    From ISA table, at h=9 km,

    ρ9km​=0.46706 m3/kg

    Thrust specific fuel consumption of aircraft,

    ct​=0.69 N/N/hr=191.67×10−6 N/N/s

    Assume aircraft is able to reach its destination airport.
    Based on this assumption, compute the fuel required.

    Equation for maximum range,

    Rmax​=ct​2​ρS2​​CD​CL​​​(W0​​−W1​​)

    Maximum ratio of CL​​ to CD​,

    CD​CL​​​=43​(3kCD0​​31​)1/4

    CD​CL​​​=43​[3(0.08)(0.015)31​]1/4

    CD​CL​​​=25

    Weight of aircraft with empty fuel tanks,

    7460×103=191.67×10−62(25)​0.46706(89.5)2​​(326110​−W1​​)

    W1​=193882.77 N

    Weight of fuel required,

    Wf​=W0​−W1​

    Wf​=326110−193882.77

    Wf​=132227.23 N

    Since the maximum fuel the aircraft can carry is 130530 N,
    it does not have sufficient fuel to reach its destination airport.

    #Part (ii)

    Maximum range achievable,

    Rmax​=191.67×10−62(25)​0.46706(89.5)2​​(326110​−326110−130530​)

    Rmax​=7350270 m

    Remaining distance to destination,

    d=(7460×103)−7350270

    d=109730.08 m

    Distance to cover as a glider.

    Maximum range of glide flight,

    Rmax​=2kCD0​​​h​

    Rmax​=20.08(0.015)​9000​

    Rmax​=129903.81 m

    Since d<Rmax(glide)​, the aircraft is able to reach its
    destination by flying as a glider after consuming its fuel.

    Glide angle required,

    tanγ=dh​=109730.089000​

    γ=4.6889°

    γ=0.081836 rad

    Alternative equation for glide angle,

    γ=LD​=CL​CD​​=CL​0.015+0.08CL​2​

    Note that equation is based on small angle approximation.
    Thus, the glide angle must be expressed in radians.

    Expressing as a quadratic equation,

    0.081836=CL​0.015+0.08CL​2​

    0=0.08CL​2−0.081836CL​+0.015

    CL1​=0.7837

    CL2​=0.23925

    Angle of attack for CL1​,

    CL1​=CLα​(α−α0​)

    0.7837=0.095(α1​+1.25°)

    α1​=7°

    Angle of attack for CL2​,

    CL2​=CLα​(α2​−α0​)

    0.23925=0.095(α2​+1.25°)

    α2​=1.2684°

    Recommended angle of attack would be α2​. In the event of an up gust, the effective α of the aircraft will increase. Thus, if the initial angle is higher, the aircraft’s α may increase beyond its stall angle, causing it to stall.

    #Part (b)

    Equation of a straight line,

    h=m(R/C)+c

    h=0−2.514000−12000​dtdh​+c

    h=−800dtdh​+c

    Note that rate of climb can be

    over change in time.

    At h=14 km, dtdh​=0.

    c=14000

    Time required to reach given altitude,

    h=−800dtdh​+14000

    dtdh​=80014000−h​

    dt=14000−h800​ dh

    t=∫09000​14000−h800​ dh

    t=800[−ln(14000−h)]09000​

    t=823.70 s

    Maximum climb rate at sea level is where h=0.

    0=−800dtdh​+14000

    dtdh​=17.5 m/s

    #Part (ii)

    Equation for net driving force,

    Fnet​=Wsinθ−D−μr​(Wcosθ−L)

    Fnet​=Wsinθ−qSCD​−μr​Wcosθ+μr​qSCL​

    Fnet​=W(sinθ−μr​cosθ)−qS(CD0​​+kCL​2)+μr​SqCL​

    Fnet​=W(sinθ−μr​cosθ)−qSCD0​​−qSkCL​2+μr​qSCL​

    Differentiating the above with respect to CL​ and equating to zero,

    dCL​dF​=−2qSkCL​+μr​qS

    0=−2qSkCL​+μr​qS

    CL​=2kμr​​

    #Part (iii)

    From Part (i),

    ρ3km​=0.90926 m3/kg

    VLO​=33.524 m/s

    Veff​=23.705 m/s

    Optimal value of lift coefficient,

    CL​=2(0.05)0.06​=0.6

    Drag during ground run,

    D=21​(0.90926)(23.705)2(16)[0.03+0.05(0.6)2]

    D=196.20 N

    Lift during ground run,

    L=2452.5 N

    sg​=2507.2+33.524

    sg​=2540.7 m

    Since the required distance is less than available
    distance of 2700m, the pilot’s idea will work.

    #Part (b)

    From the graph, at V=70 m/s,

    dtdh​=6.2593 m/s

    A portion of the aircraft’s energy is used to accelerate the aircraft. Thus, the
    instantaneous climb rate is less than the maximum climb rate achievable.

    • Vertical velocity vector Vv​=6.2593 m/s
